The lower parameter endpoint and an exact compatible negative-certificate interface
11 November 2026 Brisbane

1. Original density and the exact endpoint split.

Write u=|F_col1|²,v=|F_col2|²,j=det F and retain

 J_k(F)=j²+(3k-1)Q_k(F),
 Q_k(F)=(ku-v+2j)²/[8(k+1)]+uv/4.

Let k0=1/3. Then Q_0 here denotes Q_(1/3), not Q at parameter zero:

 Q_0(F)=[u²+18uv+9v²+12ju-36jv+36j²]/96.

This polynomial is nonnegative, being the endpoint square/product expression. It is bounded above by (7/16)|F|⁴. No quasiconvexity of Q_0 is assumed.

Fix any REAL constant A and an ACTUAL periodic phi in W^(1,4)(T2;R2). Set F=A+Dphi and

 V=integral(det F-det A)²,
 E=integral|F|⁴+|A|⁴,
 a=Q_0(A)-integral Q_0(F).

Compatibility implies integral det F=det A, so exactly

 integral(det F)²-(det A)²=V.

The variance V uses the TOTAL Jacobian. It is not ||det Dphi||², and neither constant total determinant nor small V is inferred from an arbitrary matrix measure.

2. Uniform paid remainder in k.

For 1/3<=k<=1, put S=u+v and w=ku-v+2j. Since |j|<=S/2, |w|<=2S and k+1>=4/3. Direct differentiation gives

 partial_k Q_k =wu/[4(k+1)]-w²/[8(k+1)²],

 |partial_k Q_k(F)| <= (3/8+9/32)|F|⁴
                         =(21/32)|F|⁴ <=|F|⁴.

Consequently, for h=k-1/3 in [0,2/3],

 |integral Q_k(F)-Q_k(A)+a|<=h E.

The ORIGINAL gap therefore has the two-sided, uniform, fully quantified expansion

 |[integral J_(1/3+h)(F)-J_(1/3+h)(A)]-[V-3h a]|
 <=3h² E.                                                   (1)

There is no smoothness, bounded amplitude, frequency cutoff, real oracle or stationary-PDE assumption in (1). All integrals are finite by W1,4 regularity. Strong periodic gradient approximation justifies the determinant identity and the polynomial passage.

3. An exact route from compatible constrained data to a full negative.

Suppose E>0 and a>0. Since Q_0>=0,

 a<=Q_0(A)<=(7/16)|A|⁴<=(7/16)E.

The explicit choice h=a/(2E) is thus positive and <=7/32<2/3. Formula(1) yields

 integral J_(1/3+h)(F)-J_(1/3+h)(A)
 <=V-3a²/(4E).                                              (2)

Hence the scalar inequality

 V E < (3/4)a²                                               (3)

for ONE actual compatible field supplies an admissible k=1/3+a/(2E) and a rigorously negative ORIGINAL-energy gap. This would be a full negative answer to the original universal question. It is not a negative constructed in this note:
